title: Adjoint representations, base change and tangent kernels
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $J$ be a smooth affine finitely presented $S$-group scheme. Group schemes have multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams, with the conventions of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] but with no reductivity, connectedness, torus or pinning assumption. For each commutative $A$-algebra $B$ put $L_J(B)=\ker(J(B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to J(B))$, the kernel over the identity under $\epsilon\mapsto0$ [def-sc-dual-numbers]. Its module operations are the operations on derivations at the identity: if $J=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $c:C\to B$ is the identity section, a tangent vector is $c+\epsilon d$ with $d$ $A$-linear and $d(xy)=c(x)d(y)+c(y)d(x)$. Write $L=L_J(A)$. Then $L$ is finite projective, meaning a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module, and the canonical map $B\otimes_A L\to L_J(B)$ is an isomorphism, natural under successive algebra extensions. Conjugation on dual-number points defines a homomorphism $\operatorname{Ad}_J:J\to\operatorname{GL}(L)$, where $\operatorname{GL}(L)(B)=\operatorname{Aut}_B(B\otimes_A L)$, and these homomorphisms commute with arbitrary base change. Its scheme-theoretic kernel $K=J\times_{\operatorname{GL}(L),1}S$ is an affine finitely presented closed normal subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. Normal means invariant under conjugation after every algebra extension. If $A=k$ is a field, the canonical Lie bracket and differentials of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] satisfy $d\operatorname{Ad}_J(x)(y)=[x,y]$ and identify $\operatorname{Lie}(K)=\{x\in L:[x,y]=0\text{ for all }y\in L\}$ as a subspace of $L$. No reducedness or smoothness of $K$ is required.

source.place: Introduction, printed p.2 (Lie preserves fibre products); Proposition 3.3.8 proof, printed p.102 (finite presentation of the adjoint kernel, Lie(ker Ad)=ker(ad), and functoriality). General tangent construction as in Milne, Algebraic Groups, Sections 10.19--10.23. Read online; local Conrad PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $J=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and let $u:C\to A$ be the identity augmentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $C$ is a smooth $A$-algebra. An $A$-algebra point $C\to B[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ reducing to $u_B$ has a unique expression $u_B+\epsilon d$; comparing constant and linear coefficients in the product law says precisely that $d$ is a derivation at $u_B$. Extension by $d_B(b\otimes c)=b\,d(c)$ identifies these derivations with $T(B\otimes_A C,u_B)$, with inverse restriction to $1\otimes C$. Thus [lem-sfb-smooth-augmented-tangent-scalar-extension] proves that $L=T(C,u)$ is finite projective and supplies the stated comparison, explicitly $(b\otimes d)(c)=b\,d(c)$. Its identity, tower and augmented-algebra naturality clauses give the required successive-extension compatibility, without assuming flatness of $B$.

source.place: 10.19--10.23, printed pp.192--193; agent extension to a smooth affine group over an arbitrary base ring

proof.text: For $g\in J(B)$, conjugation $c_g:J_B\to J_B$ is a scheme automorphism fixing the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $J_B=J\times_S\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$, so by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] $c_g$ is induced by an augmented $B$-algebra automorphism $q_g:B\otimes_A C\to B\otimes_A C$. The coefficient of $\epsilon$ in $c_g(u_B+\epsilon d)$ is $d\circ q_g$, which adds and scales pointwise; its inverse is the operation from $g^{-1}$. Hence conjugation is a $B$-linear automorphism of $L_J(B)$. The equality $c_{gh}=c_g\circ c_h$ proves the group homomorphism law. Under $B\to B'$, applying the algebra map to the coefficients of $g(u_B+\epsilon d)g^{-1}$ gives $g'(u_{B'}+\epsilon d')g'^{-1}$. Together with the explicit comparison in step 1 this proves naturality on all algebra points.

source.place: 10.19--10.23, printed pp.192--193; agent extension to a smooth affine group over an arbitrary base ring

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-automorphism-affine-presentation] to $P=L$. Evaluate step 2 at the universal point $g_{\rm univ}\in J(C)$, the identity map of $C$. It yields an element of $\operatorname{GL}_A(L)(C)$, hence a morphism $a:J\to\operatorname{GL}_A(L)$ by the representing bijection. Every $g\in J(B)$ is the image of this universal point under its coordinate map $C\to B$, so the naturality already proved shows $a_B(g)=\operatorname{Ad}_J(g)$. The homomorphism identities hold on universal pairs of points and thus are scheme identities. After $A\to A'$, the tangent comparisons in step 1 identify both conjugation constructions on every $A'$-algebra by the identical product $gvg^{-1}$, and the cited lemma identifies the two linear-group schemes. They therefore identify the two morphisms, compatibly with successive extensions.

source.place: 10.19--10.23, printed pp.192--193; agent extension to a smooth affine group over an arbitrary base ring

proof.text: Let $D$ be the coordinate algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_A(L)$ and $I=\ker(D\to A)$ its identity ideal, finitely generated by [lem-sfb-projective-automorphism-affine-presentation]. If $a^*:D\to C$ is step 3, then [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] describes $K$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_D A)$. This algebra is $C/(a^*(I))$: maps from either algebra to a commutative ring are exactly maps from $C$ annihilating $a^*(I)$, since $D/I=A$. Thus $K\hookrightarrow J$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its ideal is finitely generated, and $C$ is finitely presented over $A$ by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal] proves finite presentation of $K$ over $A$. This also proves finite presentation of the closed immersion, by the same finite list of ideal generators.

proof.text: For every $A$-algebra $B$, the fibre-product condition is exactly $K(B)=\{g\in J(B):\operatorname{Ad}_J(g)=1\}$. The homomorphism law gives closure under multiplication and inverse and $\operatorname{Ad}_J(hgh^{-1})=\operatorname{Ad}_J(h)1\operatorname{Ad}_J(h)^{-1}=1$. These identities on universal algebra points give a subgroup scheme and conjugation invariance, including after every algebra extension. Under any $A\to A'$, a point of the base-changed fibre product over an $A'$-algebra $B$ satisfies that same identity. Step 3 identifies it with $\operatorname{Ad}_{J_{A'}}(g)=1$. Equivalently both fibre products are the same iterated pullback: their maps into any scheme are the same compatible triples. This proves the claimed canonical kernel base-change isomorphism without a flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 022S, definition-group-scheme; agent verification of kernel and base change from the fibre-product universal property

proof.text:
Now let $A=k$ be a field. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation] choose a closed immersion $r:J\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ injective on all algebra-valued points. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus], $r(t_x)=1+\delta\,dr(x)$ and $dr$ preserves brackets, with matrix bracket $[U,V]=UV-VU$. Also $dr$ is injective: $dr(x)=0$ implies $r(t_x)=1$, hence $t_x=1$ by pointwise injectivity and then $x=0$ by the tangent identification. Write $\operatorname{Ad}_{k[\delta]}(t_x)(y)=y+\delta z$, where $k[\delta]=k[\delta]/\delta^2$; the constant term is $y$ because $t_x$ reduces to the identity. Postcomposition of coefficient derivations by $r^*$ gives $dr(y)+\delta dr(z)$, directly by linearity. In $k[\delta,\epsilon]/(\delta^2,\epsilon^2)$, apply $r$ to the conjugation defining this tangent point. The resulting matrix is
$$(1+\delta dr(x))(1+\epsilon dr(y))(1-\delta dr(x))=1+\epsilon dr(y)+\delta\epsilon[dr(x),dr(y)].$$
Comparison of the $\delta\epsilon$ coefficients gives $dr(z)=[dr(x),dr(y)]=dr([x,y])$. Injectivity of $dr$ therefore gives $z=[x,y]$. Consequently $\operatorname{Ad}_{k[\delta]}(t_x)$ acts as $1+\delta(y\mapsto[x,y])$.

source.place: Theorem 10.23 and its proof, printed p.193, equations (58)--(63); faithful representation from Theorem 4.9, p.87

proof.text: A $k[\delta]/\delta^2$-linear automorphism of $L\oplus\delta L$ reducing to $1$ has the unique form $1+\delta T$, $T\in\operatorname{End}_k(L)$, with inverse $1-\delta T$. Hence the tangent identification for the general linear group sends this automorphism to $T$. In the differential convention of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus], step 6 is precisely $d\operatorname{Ad}_J(x)(y)=[x,y]$. Finally, a tangent point $t_x$ of $J$ factors through $K$ exactly when its image in the linear group is the constant identity, by the defining fibre product. By step 6 this holds exactly when $[x,y]=0$ for every $y\in L$. Inclusion gives an injective linear map on tangent spaces (postcomposition of dual-number points); its image is the displayed subspace. Apply the cited tangent calculus to the affine finite-type group $K$ from step 4: it does not require smoothness or reducedness. This identifies its canonical $\operatorname{Lie}(K)$ with that subspace, including in positive characteristic.
